title: Zero-weight caller can spam voting-power checkpoints for any delegatee via delegate() without holding a registration or grant
description: Discovery: Lens A, GOV-02 / ZERO-WEIGHT-01 (delegation griefing, voting dust inflation). Both vaults' delegate(to) never check that msg.sender has a registration or grant. With latestVotingPower == 0 the function still executes History.push for the old delegatee (loadTop - 0) and for the new delegatee (loadTop + 0). Each call in a new block therefore appends a fresh checkpoint to the history array of any chosen address 'to' (and of the previous ghost delegatee) at zero token cost. Alternating delegate(victim) / delegate(other) lets a zero-balance attacker add one entry per block to a victim delegatee's history. Stale entries are only removed inside queryVotePower -> findAndClear -> _clear, which zeroes every stale slot in one loop (no chunking, staleBlock is fixed to block.number - staleBlockLag). If nobody calls queryVotePower for that delegatee for several thousand blocks, the single clearing loop can exceed the block gas limit, so the delegatee's queryVotePower (called by CoreVoting.vote/proposal and GSCVault membership proofs) reverts out of gas.
root_cause: delegate() does not require an existing registration/grant (nonzero latestVotingPower) and pushes a checkpoint unconditionally, even when the amount moved is 0, while the History library clears stale entries in one unbounded loop.

harm.who: Active delegatees (and their delegators) in NFTBoostVault / ARCDVestingVault
harm.loses_what: ability to cast votes or prove GSC membership through that vault until history is cleared or delegators re-delegate
harm.magnitude: temporary governance liveness loss for a targeted delegatee; attacker cost is gas only (roughly one tx per block for several thousand blocks)

exploit_trace: 1. Attacker (no tokens, no registration) calls NFTBoostVault.delegate(victim) in block N: pushes a checkpoint for address(0) and for victim (value unchanged).
2. In block N+1 attacker calls delegate(other); old delegatee victim gets another checkpoint. Repeat alternating every block for several thousand blocks.
3. Victim's history array now holds thousands of entries older than staleBlockLag that nobody cleared.
4. Victim calls CoreVoting.vote; queryVotePower -> findAndClear -> _clear must zero all stale slots in one transaction and runs out of gas.

preconditions.text: no one calls queryVotePower for the victim delegatee for a long window (thousands of blocks), so stale entries accumulate
attacker pays gas for roughly one delegate tx per block

postconditions.text: victim delegatee's queryVotePower becomes too expensive to execute; delegators must re-delegate

recommendation: Revert delegate() when the caller has no registration/grant (delegatee == address(0) / latestVotingPower == 0), and skip pushes when the moved amount is 0.

rules_applied: R10:✓(worst state is thousands of uncleared stale checkpoints)
depth_evidence: [VARIATION:ARCDVestingVault.delegate has same missing check and also lacks zero-address check on 'to']
audit_trail.missing_precondition: Requires ~6000+ blocks without any queryVotePower call on the victim; any user can call queryVotePower to clear earlier
postconditions_created: bloated checkpoint array for victim delegatee
audit_trail.who_benefits: Attacker opposing the victim delegatee's vote
